name: People and preferences
description: Who is the user, what nicknames or identities did they set, and how should the assistant address itself? Include the assistant's name, the user's relationship to the assistant, language preference, and any standing rules about tools. Prefer later explicit user decisions over the assistant introducing itself as a vendor model.
body:
# People and preferences

This document summarizes everything known about the user, their identity and preferences, and the assistant's self-presentation â as recorded in the memory bank.

## User identity

No information is recorded. Searches for user identity, name, profile, and personalization settings returned **zero observations, mental models, or memories**. The memory bank contains no statement of who the user is.

## Nicknames or identities set by the user

None are recorded. Retrieval for nicknames, identity, and "call me this name / refer to" instructions returned **no memories or chunks**. No nickname, alias, or self-chosen identity for the user exists in the memory bank.

## Assistant's name and how it should address itself

No preferred name for the assistant is recorded. Retrieval for the assistant's name, what the user should call it, and how it should refer to itself returned **no memories**.

There is also **no recorded instruction** about whether the assistant should introduce itself as a vendor model (e.g. a "Claude system prompt identity"). A dedicated query on this topic returned zero results. Consequently, there is no later explicit user decision in the memory bank that would override a vendor-model self-introduction â no such decision was ever captured.

## User's relationship to the assistant

No relationship is recorded. Queries about the relationship between the user and assistant (including a "developer" framing) returned **no memories or chunks**. Factors such as the user being a developer, a consumer, or a collaborator of the assistant are not documented.

## Language preference

No language preference is recorded. Queries for preferred language â including English, Chinese, and Japanese communication preferences â returned **no memories**. There is no basis in the memory bank for answering in one language over another for this user.

## Standing rules about tools

No standing tool rules are recorded. Queries for tool usage rules and standing instructions returned **no memories or chunks**. There is no documented rule about which tools to use, when to use them, or how to invoke them.

## Summary

The memory bank holds **no retrievable content** on any of these topics: the user's identity or nickname, the assistant's name, the user-assistant relationship, language preference, or standing tool rules. Every search â across observations, mental models, and recall â returned empty results.

Because the exact answers are not stated anywhere in the retrieved data, this document can only report the absence of information. To complete it, the following would need to be explicitly recorded in memory:

| Topic | Needed information |
|---|---|
| User identity | User's name or handle |
| Nicknames/identities | Any name or identity the user chose for themselves |
| Assistant name | What the assistant should be called, or whether it should self-identify as a vendor model |
| Relationship | How the user relates to the assistant (e.g. developer, end user, collaborator) |
| Language | Preferred response language(s) |
| Tool rules | Any standing instructions on tool usage |

Until such information is stored, no user profile, personalization, or assistant naming preference can be asserted.
